**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 9 already delivers our preferred T4C position on both halves of the rule:

| Requirement | Preferred position | Document |
|---|---|---|
| Customer convenience right | Yes | § 9.4 — "without cause", Agreement or any Order Form |
| Notice period | 30 days | § 29.4 — thirty days |
| Prepaid fee refund | Pro-rata | § 9.4 + § 10.2 |
| Early-termination fee | None | None present |
| Vendor convenience right | None mid-term | None — breach/insolvency only |

The one point worth flagging as a drafting observation (not a deviation): the notice period in § 9.4 is not stated inline but buried as a cross-reference into the *Notices* section (§ 29.4). It happens to resolve to thirty days, so the substance is correct, but that placement is unusual and easy to lose in later amendment rounds. If the negotiation reopens Section 9 or 29 for any other reason, it would be worth folding "thirty (30) days'" directly into § 9.4 as housekeeping — though it does not justify spending a redline on its own.

Two items surfaced during the sweep that fall outside this rule and should be picked up by their own playbook rules if not already covered:

- **§ 7.7** imposes liquidated damages of *fifteen percent of annual Fees per week* an invoice remains unpaid, starting ten days after the due date. This is a late-payment provision rather than a termination penalty, so it is not a T4C deviation — but it is an extremely aggressive one-way charge against us and almost certainly a high-severity issue under the fees/late-payment rule.
- **§ 8.1** sets a three-year term with **§ 8.2** auto-renewing Order Forms in twelve-month increments; the auto-renewal mechanics are Customer-favourable here (thirty days' notice plus a reminder obligation), but they belong to the term/renewal rule.
